shlokas.sanskrit: तं शयानं नरव्याघ्रं निद्रा नाभ्यागमत्तदा । चिन्तयन्तमनेकार्थं रामगीतमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.72.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ śayānaṃ naravyāghraṃ nidrā nābhyāgamattadā | cintayantamanekārthaṃ rāmagītamanuttamam || 7.72.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: As that tiger among men lay down, sleep did not come to him then, for he was pondering over the many meanings of that incomparable song of Rama.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य शब्दं सुमधुरं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम् । श्रुत्वा रात्रिर्जगामाशु शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.72.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya śabdaṃ sumadhuraṃ tantrīlayasamanvitam | śrutvā rātrirjagāmāśu śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.72.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that very sweet sound, accompanied by the rhythm of strings, the night passed swiftly for the great-souled Shatrughna.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्यां निशायां व्युष्टायां कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकं क्रमम् । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नो मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।। 7.72.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasyāṃ niśāyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ kramam | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ śatrughno munipuṅgavam || 7.72.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When that night had dawned, having performed the morning rites, Shatrughna with folded hands spoke these words to that bull among sages:

shlokas.sanskrit: भगवन्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवं रघुनन्दनम् । त्वया ऽनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि सहैभिः संशितव्रतैः ।। 7.72.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bhagavandraṣṭumicchāmi rāghavaṃ raghunandanam | tvayā 'nujñātumicchāmi sahaibhiḥ saṃśitavrataiḥ || 7.72.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O blessed one, I wish to behold Raghava, the delight of the Raghus. I wish to be granted leave by you, together with these men of firm vows."

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्येवंवादिनं तं तु शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम् । वाल्मीकिः सम्परिष्वज्य विससर्ज च राघवम् ।। 7.72.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityevaṃvādinaṃ taṃ tu śatrughnaṃ śatrutāpanam | vālmīkiḥ sampariṣvajya visasarja ca rāghavam || 7.72.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: As Shatrughna, the scorcher of foes, spoke in this manner, Valmiki embraced him and gave the descendant of Raghu leave to depart.

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं रथमारुह्य सुप्रभम् । अयोध्यामगमत्तूर्णं राघवोत्सुकदर्शनः ।। 7.72.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'bhivādya muniśreṣṭhaṃ rathamāruhya suprabham | ayodhyāmagamattūrṇaṃ rāghavotsukadarśanaḥ || 7.72.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having saluted that best of sages and mounted his splendid chariot, he went swiftly to Ayodhya, eager to behold Raghava.

shlokas.sanskrit: स प्रविष्टः पुरीं रम्यां श्रीमानिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्यत्र रामो महाद्युतिः ।। 7.72.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa praviṣṭaḥ purīṃ ramyāṃ śrīmānikṣvākunandanaḥ | praviveśa mahābāhuryatra rāmo mahādyutiḥ || 7.72.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That illustrious delight of the Ikshvakus, having entered the lovely city, the mighty-armed one went in to where Rama of great splendor was.

shlokas.sanskrit: स रामं मन्त्रिमध्यस्थं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननम् । पश्यन्नमरमध्यस्थं सहस्रनयनं यथा ।। 7.72.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rāmaṃ mantrimadhyasthaṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanam | paśyannamaramadhyasthaṃ sahasranayanaṃ yathā || 7.72.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: He gazed upon Rama, seated in the midst of his ministers, his face like the full moon, as one might behold the thousand-eyed Indra seated in the midst of the gods.

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् ।। 7.72.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ jvalantamiva tejasā | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam || 7.72.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having saluted that great soul, who blazed as it were with splendor, Shatrughna, with joined palms, spoke these words to Rama, whose valor was true.

shlokas.sanskrit: यदाज्ञप्तं महाराज सर्वं तत्कृतवानहम् । हतः स लवणः पापः पुरी चास्य निवेशिता ।। 7.72.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yadājñaptaṃ mahārāja sarvaṃ tatkṛtavānaham | hataḥ sa lavaṇaḥ pāpaḥ purī cāsya niveśitā || 7.72.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Whatever you commanded, O great king, all of that I have accomplished: the wicked Lavana has been slain, and his city has been settled and established.

shlokas.sanskrit: द्वादशैते गता वर्षास्त्वां विना रघुनन्दन । नोत्सहेयमहं वस्तुं त्वया विरहितो नृप ।। 7.72.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dvādaśaite gatā varṣāstvāṃ vinā raghunandana | notsaheyamahaṃ vastuṃ tvayā virahito nṛpa || 7.72.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: These twelve years have passed away apart from you, O delight of the Raghus; I cannot bear to dwell separated from you, O king.

shlokas.sanskrit: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम । मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम् ।। 7.72.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa me prasādaṃ kākutstha kuruṣvāmitavikrama | mātṛhīno yathā vatso na ciraṃ pravasāmyaham || 7.72.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Show me your favor, O Kakutstha of measureless might; like a calf bereft of its mother, let me not dwell abroad for long.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं शत्रुघ्नं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत् । मा विषादं कृथाः शूर नैतत्क्षत्रियचेष्टितम् ।। 7.72.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ śatrughnaṃ pariṣvajyedamabravīt | mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ śūra naitatkṣatriyaceṣṭitam || 7.72.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: To Shatrughna, who spoke thus, Rama, embracing him, said this: "Do not give way to grief, O hero; this is not the conduct of a Kshatriya."

shlokas.sanskrit: नावसीदन्ति राजानो विप्रवासेषु राघव । प्रजा नः परिपाल्या हि क्षत्रधर्मेण राघव ।। 7.72.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nāvasīdanti rājāno vipravāseṣu rāghava | prajā naḥ paripālyā hi kṣatradharmeṇa rāghava || 7.72.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Kings do not sink down despondent during their absences abroad, O Raghava; for our subjects must be protected by us according to the Kshatriya's dharma, O Raghava."

shlokas.sanskrit: काले काले तु मां वीर अयोध्यामवलोकितुम् । आगच्छ त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गन्तासि च पुरं तव ।। 7.72.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kāle kāle tu māṃ vīra ayodhyāmavalokitum | āgaccha tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gantāsi ca puraṃ tava || 7.72.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "From time to time, O hero, O best of men, come to look upon me in Ayodhya, and then you shall return to your own city."

shlokas.sanskrit: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः । अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम् ।। 7.72.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: mamāpi tvaṃ sudayitaḥ prāṇairapi na saṃśayaḥ | avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca rājyasya paripālanam || 7.72.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You too are dearer to me than my very life, of this there is no doubt; yet the governance of a kingdom must without fail be carried out."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रमिहावस । ऊर्ध्वं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.72.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasmāttvaṃ vasa kākutstha saptarātramihāvasa | ūrdhvaṃ gantāsi madhurāṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ || 7.72.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Therefore dwell here, O Kakutstha; abide here for seven nights, and afterward you shall go to Madhura together with your attendants, your army, and your conveyances."

shlokas.sanskrit: रामस्यैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तं मनोगतम् । शत्रुघ्नो दीनया वाचा बाढमित्येव चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.72.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāmasyaitadvacaḥ śrutvā dharmayuktaṃ manogatam | śatrughno dīnayā vācā bāḍhamityeva cābravīt || 7.72.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard these words of Rama, righteous and from the heart, Shatrughna, in a sorrowful voice, said only, "So be it."

shlokas.sanskrit: सप्तरात्रं च काकुत्स्थो राघवस्य यथाज्ञया । उष्य तत्र महेष्वासो गमनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.72.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: saptarātraṃ ca kākutstho rāghavasya yathājñayā | uṣya tatra maheṣvāso gamanāyopacakrame || 7.72.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the mighty archer Kakutstha, in accordance with Raghava's command, having stayed there for seven nights, made ready to depart.

shlokas.sanskrit: आमन्त्र्य तु महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् । भरतं लक्ष्मणं चैव महारथमुपारुहत् ।। 7.72.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āmantrya tu mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam | bharataṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva mahārathamupāruhat || 7.72.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having taken leave of the great-souled Rama, whose valor was true, and of Bharata and Lakshmana, he mounted his great chariot.

shlokas.sanskrit: दूरमाभ्यामनुगतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । भरतेन च शत्रुघ्नो जगामाशु पुरं ततः ।। 7.72.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dūramābhyāmanugato lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā | bharatena ca śatrughno jagāmāśu puraṃ tataḥ || 7.72.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Followed for a long way by the great-souled Lakshmana and by Bharata, Shatrughna then swiftly went on to his city.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 72 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe dvisaptatitamaḥ sargaḥ || 72 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus in the sacred Shrimad Ramayana, the first poem composed by Valmiki, in the venerable Uttara Kanda, ends the seventy-second sarga.
